newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: SOCCER-ZAMBIA CLOSE TO WINNING COSAFU CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ZAMBIA CLOSE TO WINNING COSAFU CUP.

text.p: Striker Frazier Kamwandi scored twice to lead Zambia to a 2-1 win over Mozambique on Saturday and put his country within one point of winning the inaugural Cosafa Castle Cup.

Kamwandi, who made his international debut only two months ago, put his team in the lead five minutes after half-time and then headed home an 81st minute winner to give Zambia top place in the standings of the new southern African tournament.
Zambia now just need to draw away against Namibia on August 31 to win the trophy.
But the youthful Zambian team, with just two foreign-based professionals in their line-up, were fortunate to come away with the three points after a spirited display from the Mozambicans.

Kamwandi's first goal came from close range after a defensive lapse but Mozambique equalised straight from the kick-off with a rasping shot by midfielder Sergio Faife from the edge of the penalty area.
Mozambique then created several other scoring opportunities with Sergio Faife squandering the best with a misguided header at the back post.
Zambia's 14-year unbeaten home record in competitive internationals looked distinctly shaky until a flick-on from a long throw-in allowed Kamwandi to score the winner.

The Zambians now have seven points from their three matches in the final round group competition, two more than second-placed Namibia. The two teams meet in the final match of the five-nation tournament at the end of the month.
Mozambique will finish third, with Malawi and Tanzania fighting to avoid bottom place in Lilongwe next Saturday.

Zambia - 16-Davies Phiri; 7-Elijah Tana, 19-Hilary Makasa, 2-Harrison Chongo, 12-Allan Kamwanga; 15-John Lungu, 11-Freddie Mwila junior (5-Douglas Chiwaya 79th minute), 4-Kenneth Malitoli, 14-Perry Mutapa; 9-Fraizer Kamwandi, 8-Masauso Tembo (10-Vincet Mutale 56th).

Mozambique - 12-Rui Evora; 18-Joao Chissano (10-Daniel 68th), 3-Ze Augusto, 17-Luis, 5-Tomas, 14-Pinto Barros; 2-Sergio Faife, 6-Paulito, 16-Nana; 15-Adelino (13-Mavo 86th), 9-Tico-Tico (8-Riquito 86th).
